_comment: Single source-of-truth for VaultSigner's user-facing strings (spec §9). Keys are semantic (not raw English text) so ICU MessageFormat features like plurals/gender can be added per-key without renaming call sites. Generate platform-native formats from this file with i18n/generate-apple-strings.py (and future per-platform equivalents) rather than hand-editing .strings/.xml/.resx directly. This file currently covers only the screens migrated so far (Welcome, Import Packet, the master-key-duality screen) — see /PROGRESS.md item 2.9 for what's not yet migrated. Product/brand names ("VaultSigner") are deliberately excluded, per standard i18n practice.
welcome.subtitle: Create a new vault, or open one you already have.
import.title: Import Packet
import.subtitle: Choose a .vltkey or .vltpack file.
import.transfer_password_prompt: This packet is protected by a transfer password.
duality.header: This import includes another vault's master key
duality.subtitle: Before any keys are merged, choose what to do with the incoming master key. This choice cannot be skipped.
duality.option1.title: Re-encrypt & discard incoming master key
duality.option1.description: Your keys will only need your existing master password. The imported vault's master password will not be kept.
duality.option1.no_unlocked_compartment: No compartment is currently unlocked to merge into.
duality.option2.title: Keep both master keys side by side
duality.option2.description: You'll keep two separate master passwords for this vault, one for each set of keys. Nothing is merged.
duality.option2.passphrase_field: New master passphrase for this compartment
duality.option3.title: Replace local master key with incoming master key
duality.option3.description: This will replace the password protecting ALL your existing keys, including ones you did not just import, with a different password. If you don't have both passwords available right now, stop.
